{clan_hall}Gran salón del clan
{clan_hall_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{clan_hall_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{clan_hall_northern_european}Gran salón del clan
{clan_hall_northern_european_desc}Enedwaith es una tierra de muchos clanes. Algunos pescan, otros cultivan y otros se arman para luchar contra otros clanes. Cuando se producen acontecimientos o hay que tomar decisiones que afectan a Enedwaith, los distintos caciques se reúnen en el Gran Salón del Clan. La violencia está prohibida dentro del Salón, y aquellos que infrinjan esta norma serán castigados severamente. Algunos lo consideran la sede del poder dentro de Enedwaith, ya que el clan más poderoso, Lugiu, se sienta a la cabeza de la enorme mesa que hay en su interior.\n\nEn el salón también se debaten los planes para unir Enedwaith. Aquí se acuerda formalmente que las siguientes regiones deben sucumbir al poder del Gran Salón del Clan para alzarse como una sola nación:\nNêlchelyn, Maolfinn, Caladir, Eryn Vorn, Angren Bay, Parth Iaur, Cairill, Drúwaith Iaur, Maolrunaidh, Saralainn, Heorotscir, Lugiu, Larfearann, Tierras Brunas bajas, Frontera de las Tierras Brunas y Tierras Brunas interiores.
{clan_hall_northern_european_desc_short}Grandes salones donde se reúnen los clanes de Enedwaith.

{great_clan_hall}Salón del clan maestro
{great_clan_hall_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{great_clan_hall_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{great_clan_hall_northern_european}Salón del clan maestro
{great_clan_hall_northern_european_desc}Con la consolidación de Enedwaith en una nación unificada bajo el gran Señor de la Asamblea, se necesitan más asientos en la mesa de la Asamblea y una gran estructura que sirva de monumento a esta increíble hazaña. El Salón del Clan Maestro se construirá en el emplazamiento del antiguo Salón del Clan y albergará a muchos visitantes, viajeros y guerreros. En este centro de unidad arderán hogueras, las forjas trabajarán día y noche y todos los habitantes del gran reino de los "hombres salvajes" se reunirán para enseñar y aprender. Desde aquí, Enedwaith se extenderá por toda la tierra.
{great_clan_hall_northern_european_desc_short}Centro de poder de los habitantes de Enedwaith y lugar donde se celebra la asamblea anual de clanes.

{enedwaith_union_hall}Salón del gremio de Enedwaith
{enedwaith_union_hall_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_union_hall_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{enedwaith_union_hall_northern_european}Salón del gremio de Enedwaith
{enedwaith_union_hall_northern_european_desc}Ahora que todo Enedwaith lucha bajo un mismo estandarte, los líderes de cada clan han aprobado la construcción de varios Salones del Gremio. En estos salones, mucha gente se reúne para compartir historias de sus clanes, enseñar y aprender unos de otros y estrechar lazos en toda la nación. El gran número de hábiles artesanos que acuden a estas estructuras contribuye a fomentar la causa de los clanes. Viéndose a sí mismos como un gran gremio colectivo, los hombres de Enedwaith adoptan el nombre de Gremios y se mantienen unidos utilizando estas grandes estructuras como símbolos de unidad.
{enedwaith_union_hall_northern_european_desc_short}Grandes salones donde se reúnen los mensajeros de los clanes y la gente se reúne para compartir cultura.

{barrow_downs_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barrow_downs_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barrow_downs_northern_european}Túmulos
{barrow_downs_northern_european_desc}Estas criptas embrujadas fueron en su día un lugar sagrado de enterramiento númenóreano en el reino septentrional de Cardolan. Maldecidos por el Rey Brujo de Angmar, ahora están habitados por malvados espectros que se aprovechan de cualquiera que ose invadir los antiguos túmulos. A los que viven cerca de los túmulos les resulta difícil sentirse seguros con una presencia tan maligna cerca.
{barrow_downs_northern_european_desc_short}Antiguas criptas encantadas por espectros.

{motte_and_bailey_northern_european_desc}La "mota" es un montículo elevado de tierra coronado por una sencilla torre de madera, mientras que la "liza" es una zona más amplia delimitada por una empalizada de troncos con un foso exterior. A veces, los componentes de madera se "prefabrican" fuera del emplazamiento y se llevan con un ejército para su rápida construcción. Curiosamente, la palabra "mota" acabó convirtiéndose en "foso", la profunda zanja que rodea un castillo en lugar de la propia colina artificial.

Their tongue and ours are mutually intelligible.\n\n We've bested them, though their warriors fought hard and well. The Gurach has hence decided to not make them slaves, but friends. Oaths of allegiance were exchanged, knees bent, and hostages given.\n\nUnder this arrangement, this tribe rules itself, upholds its own laws, and keeps its warriors strong.\n\nBut in exchange for this leniency, they now fight for us, when the Gurach calls them. They keep the peace and do not treat with outsiders without consulting us first. Our enemies are theirs, and theirs are ours. In time, closer ties may yet be forged, but for now they are our vassals, and gladly so.

{military_camp_northern_european}Campamento militar
{military_camp_northern_european_desc}What started out as a small mustering camp to protect the gathered farmers of the local area has grown into a far more accomplished structure, funded by the now wealthier merchants who rose out of the farmer class. A Muster Ground will help to defend against roaming rebels and put down civil strife amongst the wild folk but a Military Camp helps to prepare the Wildmen for the wider world and the inevitability of war, whilst still maintaining sharp order. With many more pastures and a large stables, more horsemen can effectively be equipped here; a larger archery range allows for the recruitment of more bow armed warriors and a grand drinking hall with many beds provides for a larger amount of foot soldiers. For the Wildmen to stamp out their enemies, a Military Camp is essential to any community.
{military_camp_northern_european_desc_short}The Military Camp allows the Wildmen to prepare for war against the stronger factions of Middle-earth.

The process of selecting a leader for each cohort is most time consuming part, as up and coming Serpent Warriors vie for a chance at command. Competition within the Harad's military is vicious and unpredictable. The wise ones of the new recruits will begin to shed their tribal identities and become increasingly familiar with their comrades, so that they may better outlive them and gain the most from their share of the plunder.

The warehouses belong to the Serpent Tribe Syndicate — the merchant collective that answers to the master of Harad. Because sea trade is often a joint effort by multiple tribes it can quickly become subject to disputes over goods and profit distribution. The Syndicate effectively makes itself available for the housing of goods and their transportation, taking a hefty portion of the goods for themselves. \n\nThese goods are either sold or held until they bring in the most profit. The Serpent Lord reaps what is effectively a tax on all sea trade, while ensuring the price of goods remain under his control. The master of Harad keeps a tight hold on foreign exchange so that it does not upset his control over Harad's economy. Any tribe or trader who would attempt to avoid the Syndicate will find themselves at the wrong end of a Serpent Warrior's blade.

{corn_exchange_spain}Intercambiador de alimentos
{corn_exchange_spain_desc}A Food Exchange is the most efficient way for food to be distributed to the tribes of a province. It is effectively a large public granary every local tribe can access for the purchase and retail of food and produce. From here goods are sold and transported to the smaller tribal markets and pantries.\n\nDespite what some northern realms may think; the people of Harad eat well and have a large selection of fruits, meats, grains, and vegetables available. Their warm and diverse climate offers several growing seasons and the vast fertile river lands of the Harnen yields plentiful crops. Their abundance is what has given rise to the Haradwaith; the Southern Multitude. The Serpent Lord takes full advantage of the surplus of food and his army never wants for supply nor manpower. Wild game and domestic animals both provide meat, irrigated farms produce grain and barley for bread. Apples, peaches, olives, and grapes are abundant in the south. Even heartier vegetables from the north have found their way to the market and fields; likely as plunder by a particularly cunning warrior. {c_town_hall_spain}Oficina de reclutamiento tribal
{c_town_hall_spain_desc}This building handles the extraction of manpower from local tribes. Each tribe is taxed a quota of able men to join the army of Harad. These troops typically need little training, the Haradrim tribes are proud warriors and their men are expected to learn combat skills at an early age. The tribes are also expected to provide their warriors with weapons, clothing, equipment, and enough provisions to last them several months. This ensures the cost of these new warriors is minimal and they can be deployed to the front lines immediately. \n\nEven a small settlement maintains a Conscription Office and they can be found across Harad. Fresh recruits are often expected to camp on office grounds until they are sent on deployment. Serpent Warriors are often seen here, managing the new troops and bringing in men from their respective tribes. \n\nAnd in the shadows, watching for signs of disloyalty or treachery, lurk the Hasarii.

{c_sawmill_desc}A Sawmill is a building where timber is stored and processed so it can be used for other works like for buildings and parts of armour for units. This increased efficiency of manufacture of wood through higher rates of logging allows the armies to grow faster and to be re-fitted with new equipment after battles. This structure can be upgraded further into a Lumber Yard.
{c_sawmill_desc_short}A Sawmill is a structure which will aid in the processing of wood.
{c_lumber_yard}Asserradero
{c_lumber_yard_desc}A Lumber Yard is a place where timber is stored and processed for the use in buildings and armour. The advanced structure of the buildings allows it to process wood very quickly meaning even more workers can be sent to cut down the wood in the nearby forests. This refined process will greatly boost the replenish rate of the armies as well as reducing the cost of wooden buildings.
{c_lumber_yard_desc_short}A Lumber Yard is a building which will store and process wood.

{ecthelion_northern_european_desc}The White Tower of Minas Tirith. The Tower of Ecthelion is 50 fathoms (300 feet) tall. The plain white standard of the Stewards of Gondor flows from its pinnacle. The Tower stands in the centre of the Citadel on the seventh level of the city. In front of the Tower is the Court of the Fountain where the White Tree of Gondor grew.\n\nIn the Tower Hall is the throne of the King of Gondor upon a dais, and at the foot the dais on the lowest step is a black chair where the Steward of Gondor sits. There is a chamber high in the Tower and above it in the summit there is a secret room where the palantír of Minas Anor called the Anor-stone is kept.\n\nThe White Tower was first built by King Calimehtar in 1900 in order to house the palantír. In 2698, the Tower was repaired and rebuilt by the Steward Ecthelion I, for whom the Tower came to be named.\n\nThe elite military unit in Minas Tirith is called the Guard of the Citadel or the Guard of the Tower of Gondor.

{dome_stars}Cúpula de las estrellas en ruinas
{dome_stars_desc}The Dome of Stars was built in Osgiliath on top of the bridge that crossed the river Anduin. Under the great dome were the thrones of the two kings and subsequently the Kings of Gondor. This was also where the Master Stone of Osgiliath, the chief palantír of Gondor, was kept. The tower was destroyed in TA 1437 when Castamir the Usurper and his men sieged and burned Osgiliath during the Kin-strife. The palantír kept inside it was forever lost beneath surface of the river Anduin in TA 1437.
{dome_stars_desc_short}The Dome of Stars was a great domed hall in Osgiliath before the kin-strife that housed one of the Palantiri

The tower was destroyed in TA 1437 when Castamir the Usurper and his men sieged and burned Osgiliath during the Kin-strife. The palantír kept inside it was forever lost beneath surface of the river Anduin in TA 1437.

{orthanc_northern_european}Orthanc
{orthanc_northern_european_desc}Within the Ring of Isengard is a large circular plain. The ground dips slightly to form a shallow bowl, at the centre of which stands the Tower of Orthanc. Orthanc was made of hard, gleaming black stone. The Tower was man-made but appeared like a great spur of rock thrusting out of the plain.\n\nIt is composed of four, many-sided columns of rock joined together that rose to a height of 500 feet and then fork into four sharp pinnacles. Between the pinnacles is a small roof of polished stone carved with astronomical signs where a person can stand and watch the stars. This platform can be reached by a single staircase of many thousand steps inside the Tower.\n\nThe only door into Orthanc is on the eastern side, in the angle of two of the stone columns. The Keys of Orthanc are used to lock this door. A flight of 27 stone steps leads up to the door. Above the door is a balcony with an iron railing, and a shuttered window opened onto the balcony. There are many more tall windows around the Tower of Orthanc, even in the four pinnacles.
{orthanc_northern_european_desc_short}The central tower of Isengard.

{dragon_inn_northern_european}Dragón verde
{dragon_inn_northern_european_desc}The Green Dragon is the last building on the side of Bywater nearest to Hobbiton. It is located on the Bywater Road which links with the Great East Road. Hobbits from Bywater, Hobbiton, and the surrounding area come to the Green Dragon for pints of beer and gossip.\n\nOn April 27, 2941, at the beginning of the quest to the Lonely Mountain, Thorin and Company went ahead to the Green Dragon to make preparations and await Bilbo Baggins.\n\nOne evening in early April of 3018, Sam Gamgee and Ted Sandyman, the miller's son, were at the Green Dragon. Sam spoke of strange things that had been happening, such as queer folk passing through the Shire and the Tree-man his cousin Hal claimed to have seen on the North Moors. Sam was particularly sad about the passing of the Elves westward as they left Middle-earth. Ted Sandyman scoffed at Sam's tales.
{dragon_inn_northern_european_desc_short}The Green Dragon is a popular inn near Hobbiton.

{pony_northern_european}Poni Pisador
{pony_northern_european_desc}The Prancing Pony is a meeting place for both Bree-folk and travellers on the Great East Road and the Greenway. The inn is a place to hear news of the outside worlds and is frequented by Men, Hobbits, Dwarves, and the occasional Wizard. The art of smoking pipe-weed is said to have begun in Bree and from the Prancing Pony it spread among the races of Middle-earth. The inn is also noted for its fine beer.\n\nIt is located on the Great East Road at the base of Bree-hill. The front of the inn faces the Road and an archway leads to a courtyard between two wings that runs back into the hill. The main door is to the left of the archway. A sign hangs over the door with a painting of a rearing pony and the words The Prancing Pony by Barliman Butterbur. Inside there is a large Common Room, several private parlours, and a number of bedrooms, including a few rooms in the north wing designed for Hobbits that are low to the ground and have round windows. The inn also had stables.
{pony_northern_european_desc_short}The Prancing Pony is a famous inn in Bree.

{tirith_aear}The Tirith Aear
{tirith_aear_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{tirith_aear_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{tirith_aear_northern_european}Tirith Aear
{tirith_aear_northern_european_desc}The Tirith Aear, literally translated as 'Sea Guard' but known as 'Seaward', is a tall and proud tower constructed in the Castle-city of Dol Amroth to serve as a beacon of strength to all those who look upon it. Although tall, gleaming white and visible for miles around, the tower did not act as a lighthouse but rather as a bell tower, chiming to mark day to day business of Dol Amroth or in appreciation of grand events such as the marriages of two daughters of the city; Finduilas to Steward Denethor II and Lothíriel to Éomer, King of the Mark. The origin of the tower is unknown but many suggest it was constructed so that should Lord Amroth ever return to shore he would have a guide by which to do so.
{tirith_aear_northern_european_desc_short}The Tirith Aear is a mighty tower constructed in the Castle-city of Dol Amroth.

{amon_sul}Atalaya de Amon Sûl
{amon_sul_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{amon_sul_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{amon_sul_northern_european}Atalaya de Amon Sûl
{amon_sul_northern_european_desc}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl was built in the days of Elendil at the dawn of the Third Age and was constructed atop the strategically important hill know as Weathertop in westron and Amon Sûl in Sindarin (literally 'windy hill'). Weathertop lies at the southernmost tip of the Weather Hills and is the highest peak for miles around and it was there that the Palantir of the north was given a home; further adding to the strategic importance of the tower atop the hill. Upon Arnor's divide after the passing of King Eärendur, the hill was fiercely contested diplomatically as it stands at the intersection of three realms; Arthedain, Cardolan and Rhudaur, however the hill passed into the control of Arthedain and developed strong ties with the northern third of old Arnor. In the reign of Argeleb, when the Witch-king began to grow in power and the men of Rhudaur openly contested their brothers, the tower was strengthened and became a mighty bastion against the oncoming tide of evil from the north-east, providing the headquarters of a strong line the Dúnedain set up across the Weather Hills. Amon Sûl held out for nigh on half a century but was eventually overcome by the Witch-king whereupon Arveleg, son of Argeleb, was slain. The tower was then abandoned for many years but now, as the Dúnedain continue their tireless mission of protecting Eriador, it has become a prominent staging ground for the shadowy individuals hosting many armed men of the Dúnedain 'army' and calling men from all three realms of the past.
{amon_sul_northern_european_desc_short}The Watchtower of Amon Sûl was a mighty tower constructed in the glory days of Arnor but now sits in ruin.

{hobbit}hobbit
{hobbit_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hobbit_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hobbit_northern_european}Smials
{hobbit_northern_european_desc}Smials are hole dwellings used by Hobbits. They are composed of a tunnel or tunnels and rooms dug into the ground. Hills and banks are the most suitable locations for smials.\n\nThe tunnels of a smial are generally tube-shaped with round doors and round windows. The simplest smials have dirt walls and floors, while the better smials have panelled walls and tiled floors. Some smials are very small, while others have several branches and rooms. Brandy Hall and the Great Smials are mansions with numerous tunnels and rooms where many members of an extended family live. Bag End is an example of a large, single-family smial that has many rooms on either side of one main tunnel.\n\nHobbits have lived in smials for as far back as they could remember. The people of Rohan remember legends from when they lived in the North of the Halflings who lived in holes in sand dunes. After the Hobbits settled in the Shire, the custom of building smials remained, but Hobbits also began to build houses and other buildings above ground. By the end of the Third Age, it was generally the poorest and richest Hobbits who still dwelled in smials.
{hobbit_northern_european_desc_short}Hole dwellings used by Hobbits.

{office_northern_european}Oficina del Alcalde de Cavada Grande
{office_northern_european_desc}The office of the Mayor is an ancient building, by hobbit standards, that acts as both a popular inn and Mayoral seat of power. Originally used as simply a hall for the Mayor to house his guests when they came to speak with him, it quickly grew into a famous inn as his 'guests' would often stay for weeks. As such it has become the very centre of Michel Delving with all manner of news, and travellers, to make their way through its four walls. Whilst not being as well known as the Green Dragon or the Prancing Pony it is nevertheless an establishment held in high regard! Occasionally the Mayor does hold official gatherings here but as his power slowly passes to the thain the Office is used more and more as an inn than a grand hall.

Rumblings of the power of the Dwarves and memories of the War of the Dwarves and Orcs has given the cavern a reprieve for none but the Warlord of Gundabad has stepped foot in here since Gundabad was reclaimed for the orcs some 200 years ago.

{barad}barad_dur
{barad_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barad_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{barad_northern_european}Barad-dûr
{barad_northern_european_desc}Stronghold of Sauron in Mordor. The Dark Tower is at the end of a long spur of the Ash Mountains on the northern border of Mordor. The tower overlooks the plateau of Gorgoroth. A road leads north-west from the Dark Tower to the Black Gate, about 100 miles away. Mount Doom is about 30 miles directly west of the Dark Tower. Sauron's Road runs from the western gate of the Dark Tower over an iron bridge spanning an abyss and then across Gorgoroth to the eastern slopes of Mount Doom.\n\nThe Dark Tower is an immense fortress of immeasurable strength. It was made of iron and extremely hard stone and its gates are steel. The tower is black and it is wreathed in veils of shadow woven by Sauron. It is very tall with many walls, battlements, and towers. The highest tower is topped with an iron crown and in it is the Window of the Eye from which Sauron gazes. Within the Dark Tower are great courts and an armoury and windowless dungeons; and beneath the tower are deep pits.\n\nSauron began building the Dark Tower around the year 1000 of the Second Age, when he chose Mordor as his realm. The tower was completed around the year 1600 of the Second Age Sauron forged the One Ring in Mount Doom at this time as well, and the foundations of the Dark Tower were strengthened by the power of the Ring.\n\nSauron ruled from the Dark Tower and expanded his power in Middle-earth until he was challenged by Ar-Pharazôn, King of Númenor, in 3262 of the Second Age. Seeing the might of Ar-Pharazôn's forces, Sauron came down from the Dark Tower and allowed himself to be taken to Númenor. There he persuaded Ar-Pharazôn to defy the Valar and sail to the Undying Lands, which led to the Downfall of Númenor in 3319 of the Second Age \n\nSauron's physical body was lost in the destruction of Númenor, but his spirit returned to the Dark Tower in 3320 of the Second Age. There he took up the Ring again and assumed a new form. In the War of the Last Alliance, Elves and Men marched to war against Sauron and defeated his forces at the Battle of Dagorlad before the Black Gate in 3434 S.A. The armies of the Last Alliance then entered Mordor and besieged the Dark Tower.\n\nThe Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years. At last in 3441 of the Second Age, Sauron himself came down from his tower and fought with Gil-galad and Elendil. All three fell in that mortal contest and Isildur took the One Ring from Sauron and kept it for himself. The Dark Tower was destroyed, but the foundations could not be broken as long as the Ring survived.\n\nSauron returned around 1050 of the Third Age and established a new stronghold at Dol Guldur in Mirkwood. The White Council attacked Dol Guldur in 2941 and the next year Sauron returned in secret to Mordor. In 2951, he declared himself openly and began rebuilding the Dark Tower. Sauron has a palantír in the Dark Tower: most likely the Ithil-stone that had been taken by the Nazgûl from Minas Ithil.
{barad_northern_european_desc_short}Sauron's stronghold of immeasurable strength.
{barad_mesoamerican_desc}Stronghold of Sauron in Mordor. The Dark Tower is at the end of a long spur of the Ash Mountains on the northern border of Mordor. The tower overlooks the plateau of Gorgoroth. A road leads north-west from the Dark Tower to the Black Gate, about 100 miles away. Mount Doom is about 30 miles directly west of the Dark Tower. Sauron's Road runs from the western gate of the Dark Tower over an iron bridge spanning an abyss and then across Gorgoroth to the eastern slopes of Mount Doom.\n\nThe Dark Tower is an immense fortress of immeasurable strength. It was made of iron and extremely hard stone and its gates are steel. The tower is black and it is wreathed in veils of shadow woven by Sauron. It is very tall with many walls, battlements, and towers. The highest tower is topped with an iron crown and in it is the Window of the Eye from which Sauron gazes. Within the Dark Tower are great courts and an armoury and windowless dungeons; and beneath the tower are deep pits.\n\nSauron began building the Dark Tower around the year 1000 of the Second Age, when he chose Mordor as his realm. The tower was completed around the year 1600 of the Second Age Sauron forged the One Ring in Mount Doom at this time as well, and the foundations of the Dark Tower were strengthened by the power of the Ring.\n\nSauron ruled from the Dark Tower and expanded his power in Middle-earth until he was challenged by Ar-Pharazôn, King of Númenor, in 3262 of the Second Age. Seeing the might of Ar-Pharazôn's forces, Sauron came down from the Dark Tower and allowed himself to be taken to Númenor. There he persuaded Ar-Pharazôn to defy the Valar and sail to the Undying Lands, which led to the Downfall of Númenor in 3319 of the Second Age \n\nSauron's physical body was lost in the destruction of Númenor, but his spirit returned to the Dark Tower in 3320 of the Second Age. There he took up the Ring again and assumed a new form. In the War of the Last Alliance, Elves and Men marched to war against Sauron and defeated his forces at the Battle of Dagorlad before the Black Gate in 3434 S.A. The armies of the Last Alliance then entered Mordor and besieged the Dark Tower.\n\nThe Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years. At last in 3441 of the Second Age, Sauron himself came down from his tower and fought with Gil-galad and Elendil. All three fell in that mortal contest and Isildur took the One Ring from Sauron and kept it for himself. The Dark Tower was destroyed, but the foundations could not be broken as long as the Ring survived.\n\nSauron returned around 1050 of the Third Age and established a new stronghold at Dol Guldur in Mirkwood. The White Council attacked Dol Guldur in 2941 and the next year Sauron returned in secret to Mordor. In 2951, he declared himself openly and began rebuilding the Dark Tower. Sauron has a palantír in the Dark Tower: most likely the Ithil-stone that had been taken by the Nazgûl from Minas Ithil.

{gate}black_gate
{gate_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{gate_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{gate_northern_european}Puerta Negra
{gate_northern_european_desc}Main entrance into Mordor. The Black Gate is located at the north-western corner of Mordor. It spans Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass, at the point where the Ash Mountains met the Mountains of Shadow. Behind the Black Gate is the valley of Udûn which leads to the plain of Gorgoroth.\n\nThe Black Gate was made of iron set in a stone rampart that stretched between the high cliffs on either side of the pass. It had two great iron doors. There was a battlement across the top of the Black Gate which was patrolled by sentries. The Towers of the Teeth flanked the Black Gate: Narchost on the west, or right as one faced the Gate, and Carchost on the east or left. There were also hundreds of Orc-holes in the cliffs around the Black Gate.\n\nIn front of the Black Gate is the Desolation of the Morannon. It is a grim and barren land where nothing grows. There are mounds of blasted earth that leaks poisonous fumes. Two great Slag-hills face the Black Gate. Mires and pools of mud and oily liquid stretch before the Black Gate like a moat. Beyond the Desolation of the Morannon is Dagorlad, the great Battle Plain.\n\nThree roads converge at the Black Gate. One road comes from the north across Dagorlad. Another came from the east alongside the Ash Mountains. This road is only about 50 miles long, extending just about to the point where Barad-dûr stands on the other side of the Ash Mountains. The third road is the Harad Road which runs southward from the Black Gate through Ithilien and on to the southern lands of Harad.\n\nIt was made by Sauron sometime after he chose Mordor as his realm in 1000 of the Second Age. In 3434, the War of the Last Alliance began with the Battle of Dagorlad on the plain in front of the Black Gate. The Men and Elves of the Last Alliance defeated Sauron's forces and assaulted the Black Gate. Sauron retreated to Barad-dûr and the Army of the Last Alliance managed to enter the Black Gate behind him. The Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years until 3441 when Sauron was finally defeated.\n\nSauron's spirit fled from Mordor into the East after the One Ring was taken from him. The Men of Gondor took control of the Black Gate and they built the Towers of the Teeth on either side of it. They kept watch over the Black Gate to guard against Sauron's return.\n\nThe watch on Mordor declined after the Great Plague of 1636 which killed many Men of Gondor, but the Black Gate remained under Gondor's control until at least 1944. In that year, King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle with the Wainriders in front of the Black Gate. The watch-towers of the Black Gate were abandoned by the Men of Gondor sometime afterwards - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.
{gate_northern_european_desc_short}Black Gate, the main entrance into Mordor.

{gate_greek_desc}Main entrance into Mordor. The Black Gate is located at the north-western corner of Mordor. It spans Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass, at the point where the Ash Mountains met the Mountains of Shadow. Behind the Black Gate is the valley of Udûn which leads to the plain of Gorgoroth.\n\nThe Black Gate was made of iron set in a stone rampart that stretched between the high cliffs on either side of the pass. It had two great iron doors. There was a battlement across the top of the Black Gate which was patrolled by sentries. The Towers of the Teeth flanked the Black Gate: Narchost on the west, or right as one faced the Gate, and Carchost on the east or left. There were also hundreds of Orc-holes in the cliffs around the Black Gate.\n\nIn front of the Black Gate is the Desolation of the Morannon. It is a grim and barren land where nothing grows. There are mounds of blasted earth that leaks poisonous fumes. Two great Slag-hills face the Black Gate. Mires and pools of mud and oily liquid stretch before the Black Gate like a moat. Beyond the Desolation of the Morannon is Dagorlad, the great Battle Plain.\n\nThree roads converge at the Black Gate. One road comes from the north across Dagorlad. Another came from the east alongside the Ash Mountains. This road is only about 50 miles long, extending just about to the point where Barad-dûr stands on the other side of the Ash Mountains. The third road is the Harad Road which runs southward from the Black Gate through Ithilien and on to the southern lands of Harad.\n\nIt was made by Sauron sometime after he chose Mordor as his realm in 1000 of the Second Age. In 3434, the War of the Last Alliance began with the Battle of Dagorlad on the plain in front of the Black Gate. The Men and Elves of the Last Alliance defeated Sauron's forces and assaulted the Black Gate. Sauron retreated to Barad-dûr and the Army of the Last Alliance managed to enter the Black Gate behind him. The Siege of Barad-dûr lasted seven years until 3441 when Sauron was finally defeated.\n\nSauron's spirit fled from Mordor into the East after the One Ring was taken from him. The Men of Gondor took control of the Black Gate and they built the Towers of the Teeth on either side of it. They kept watch over the Black Gate to guard against Sauron's return.\n\nThe watch on Mordor declined after the Great Plague of 1636 which killed many Men of Gondor, but the Black Gate remained under Gondor's control until at least 1944. In that year, King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle with the Wainriders in front of the Black Gate. The watch-towers of the Black Gate were abandoned by the Men of Gondor sometime afterwards - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.
{gate_greek_desc_short}Black Gate, the main entrance into Mordor.

{teeth_northern_european}Torres de los dientes
{teeth_northern_european_desc}The Towers of the Teeth stand on either side of Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass between the Mountains of Shadow and the Ash Mountains at the north-west corner of Mordor. Carchost is on the east (or left facing the Gate) and Narchost is on the west. The Black Gate bares the pass between the two towers. The towers are tall and strong and have window-holes that face north, east and west.\n\nThe Towers of the Teeth were built by the Men of Gondor after the defeat of Sauron in the War of the Last Alliance at the end of the Second Age in order to guard against the possibility of the Dark Lord's return to Mordor. The towers were still in the control of Gondor as late as 1944 of the Third Age, when King Ondoher of Gondor was slain in battle against the Wainriders before the Black Gate. The Towers of the Teeth were deserted at some point after that - probably before 1980 when the Lord of the Nazgûl returned to Mordor.\n\nIn 2942, Sauron returned to Mordor and the Towers of the Teeth came under his control. Sauron filled the towers with garrisons of armed guards who keeps ceaseless watch on the Black Gate.

{hornburg}helms_deep
{hornburg_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hornburg_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hornburg_northern_european}Cuernavilla
{hornburg_northern_european_desc}Helm's Deep is a narrow ravine with high cliffs on the northern and southern sides that block out the sunlight. The Deeping-wall is built across the entrance to the ravine, and at the northern end of the wall is the fortress of the Hornburg. No enemy has ever captured the Hornburg while it was defended.\n\nThe Hornburg stands on a spur called the Hornrock that juts out from the northern cliff. It is surrounded by a wall, behind which is an outer court and a citadel containing an inner court and a tall tower. In the tower is the great horn of Helm Hammerhand. When the horn is sounded, it echoes throughout the ravine and causes fear and dismay among enemy forces.\n\nA causeway leads up to the Hornburg-gates. To one side of the main gate a narrow walkway leads along the edge of the Hornrock to a small postern-door into the Hornburg. There is also a rear-gate with a stairway leading down from the Hornburg into the ravine behind the Deeping-wall.\n\nThe Deeping-wall stands 20 feet high and is wide enough for four men to stand side by side. The surface of the wall is smooth and nearly seamless. There is a tall parapet on the wall with openings for archers. Three staircases lead down from the back of the wall into the ravine, and another staircase leads up into the Hornburg.\n\nBehind the Deeping-wall, the cliffs draw closer together and form the Narrows. At the far end of the Narrows is the entrance to the Glittering Caves under the Thrihyrne. The Deeping-stream flows from the caves and passes under the Deeping-wall through a small culvert and then loop around the Hornburg and under the causeway. From the Hornburg, the Deeping-road runs alongside the Deeping-stream to the Great West Road.\n\nThe fortress and the Deeping-wall were built by the Men of Gondor sometime during the reign of the Ship-kings (830-1149). Its purpose is to guard the southern side of the Gap, while Isengard guards the northern side.
{hornburg_northern_european_desc_short}The Hornburg is a stronghold that guards the southern end of the Gap of Rohan.

It is surrounded by a wall, behind which is an outer court and a citadel containing an inner court and a tall tower. In the tower is the great horn of Helm Hammerhand. When the horn is sounded, it echoes throughout the ravine and causes fear and dismay among enemy forces.\n\nA causeway leads up to the Hornburg-gates. To one side of the main gate a narrow walkway leads along the edge of the Hornrock to a small postern-door into the Hornburg. There is also a rear-gate with a stairway leading down from the Hornburg into the ravine behind the Deeping-wall.\n\nThe Deeping-wall stands 20 feet high and is wide enough for four men to stand side by side. The surface of the wall is smooth and nearly seamless. There is a tall parapet on the wall with openings for archers. Three staircases lead down from the back of the wall into the ravine, and another staircase leads up into the Hornburg.\n\nBehind the Deeping-wall, the cliffs draw closer together and form the Narrows. At the far end of the Narrows is the entrance to the Glittering Caves under the Thrihyrne. The Deeping-stream flows from the caves and passes under the Deeping-wall through a small culvert and then loop around the Hornburg and under the causeway. From the Hornburg, the Deeping-road runs alongside the Deeping-stream to the Great West Road.\n\nThe fortress and the Deeping-wall were built by the Men of Gondor sometime during the reign of the Ship-kings (830-1149). Its purpose is to guard the southern side of the Gap, while Isengard guards the northern side.
{hornburg_gondor_desc_short}The Hornburg is a stronghold that guards the southern end of the Gap of Rohan.

{hall}golden_hall
{hall_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hall_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hall_northern_european}Salón dorado de Meduseld
{hall_northern_european_desc}The Golden Hall of the Kings of Rohan, also known as Meduseld sits atop the city of Edoras, the capital of Rohan at the foot of the White Mountains. Edoras was built on a hill and Meduseld was at the summit, standing apart from the other buildings on a high platform built upon a green terrace.\n\nIts thatched roof gleams golden in the sunlight and can been seen from afar. A long, broad stair leads up the green terrace to a wide paved area in front of the door. Guards sit on seats carved from stone on either side of the top step. The doors face north and were made of wood carved with images of beasts and birds with jewelled eyes and golden claws. On either side of the doors stand pillars hewn from mighty trees carved with interlacing figures that are gilded and painted.\n\nThe interior of Meduseld is a single long room. The high roof is supported by pillars that were decorated with carvings and gold and other colours. There is a louvre in the roof that let out smoke and lets in light. Light also comes into the hall through slitted, unglazed windows under the eaves on the eastern side.\n\nOn the walls are woven cloths that depict scenes and figures from the history of the Rohirrim, including one of Eorl the Young mounted on Felarof riding to the Battle of the Field of Celebrant. There is a long hearth in the middle of the hall. At the south end of the hall facing the door is a dais with three steps. On the dais is the King's throne, which was a great gilded chair.\n\nMeduseld was built by Brego, son of Eorl and was completed in 2569. At the feast held to hallow the hall, Brego's son Baldor vowed to walk the Paths of the Dead. He never returned, and his father Brego died of grief a year later.
{hall_northern_european_desc_short}The Golden Hall is the hall of the Kings of Rohan.

{elrond_house_northern_european_desc}Home of Elrond in Rivendell. It is not known precisely when the Last Homely House was built, but Elrond established his refuge in Rivendell in 1697 of the Second Age. In addition to Elrond and his family, a number of other Elves resided or visited there. Among these were the Elf-lord Glorfindel, Elrond's counsellor Erestor, and Lindir. Aragorn was raised in the Last Homely House from 2933 to 2951 of the Third Age, and he frequently returns to visit.\n\nThe Last Homely House is located in a deep, hidden valley. There is only one path leading to the house. It passes over a narrow stone bridge without a parapet that spans one of the swift-running mountain streams that forms the River Bruinen.\n\nThe house is large and has many rooms and halls. The main room is the Hall of Fire. It was so named because of the great hearth set between two carved pillars with a fire that blazed year-round. The Hall of Fire is usually a quiet place for people to sit and think, but on high days it is filled with stories and songs.

{hunting_camp}hunting_camp
{hunting_camp_desc}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hunting_camp_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{hunting_camp_northern_european}Campamento de caza
{hunting_camp_northern_european_desc}The hunting camp is the home of the Trappermen. The camp exists out of wooden cabins and tents placed at the edge of the wild. The cabins are mostly used to preserve the fresh meat from decaying and to store their tools. The tents have the sole purpose of being a sleeping quarter for the hunters. While these men reside in the camp they learn the skills of a true hunter. With bow and arrow they hunt on the wild animals which live near the settlement and when necessary the Trappermen will take up arms to attack any orcs on their path. The addition of this food network and sleeping quarters allows the town that hosts the hunters to freely support more troops.
{hunting_camp_northern_european_desc_short}A Hunting Camp allows the recruitment of organized woodsmen.

Known as the Gwaith-i-Mírdain, this brotherhood was founded in the early centuries of the Second Age with the purpose of preserving and advancing all Ñoldorin lore of crafting and forging.\n\nTheir eagerness to explore ever deeper knowledge in these arts made them vulnerable to Sauron's deceit. He left Eregion around S.A. 1500. During his conquest of Eregion in S.A. 1697, the House of the Mírdain was his major goal. Though Celebrimbor defended it heroically, his efforts were in vain, and the brotherhood's house was looted and burned.\n\nWe will have no hope of restoring this structure to its former glory unless we can once again support the finest Elven smiths in Middle-earth. To that end, it is advised to construct and upgrade as many blacksmiths as possible, in the hope that an apprentice might arise who could rival Celebrimbor of old.

At all times, even during the wars against Morgoth in the First Age, their lore-masters invented new words. It was Rúmil of Tirion who first invented letters with which words could be written down. The Tengwar they were called by the Ñoldor. Fëanor enhanced, and for large parts invented anew, the system which was created by Rúmil. The Tengwar fëanorinwa are still popular all over Middle-earth and used these days. Accompanied with the invention of script, the Ñoldor began to keep track of the events of their time. They even recorded whatsoever account of history the Valar were willing to reveal to them. The Gwaith-i-Lúmenquentalë (History Guild) is the centre of history-lore kept by the Ñoldor. Here their lore-masters discuss about events of the past and teach the willing tales of days long forgotten in the minds of Men. The amount of knowledge stored in the Gwaith-i-Lúmenquentalë is invaluable and so are the benefits of it.

It is said, that in the Eldar in Valinor preserved songs they used to sing beneath the stars at the shores of Cuiviénen and to which they used to dance. The Teleri was the clan of the Quendi from which the greatest singers came in the old days – save only Maglor, Fëanor son, who was obviously a Ñoldor. One will seldom find a book of history amongst the Nandor and Sindar, but always will find songs of wisdom and nearly every account of history, which are performed with or without dance. The Gwaith-i-Glinadir'a'mereth is the place where the greatest singers and best performers of the Sindar and Nandor of the Realm of Thranduil come together for exchange, pleasure and celebrations. Wherever a Gwaith-i-Glinadir'a'mereth (Dance Guild) exists, it is the centre of culture not only on days of joy and celebration but in day-to-day Life.

Whether this is stamped out or used by the local lord for his own gains, is largely dependant on his own needs. {pipeweed_guild_desc}Pipe-weed (also known as Halflings' Leaf or simply Leaf) is famous across Middle-earth for its fragrant smell and calming effects when smoked. Preferring warmer climates, it can be found growing wild in many fields across Gondor and in rare, sheltered places in the north it is carefully cultivated by enthusiasts, notablly Bree-hill and Longbottom. Popular varieties of pipe-weed from the Shire include Longbottom Leaf, Old Toby, and Southern Star. Lesser known varieties like Southlinch from Bree and Stubleaf from Western Gondor have also been known to exist.\n\nA local farmer, a keen pipe-weed smoker himself, has identified some smallholdings that would be an excellent place to begin the cultivation of this strange plant. With the blessing of the local lord and a small investment, he is willing to share some of his profits and produce.
{pipeweed_guild_desc_short}A small pipe-weed farm producing a variety of leafs.

{explorers_guild_desc}• Provides watchtowers on borders in the region\n\nMiddle-earth is a wild and untamed place. Many towns and cities lie unconnected, isolated from the outside world. Messenger posts that once heralded news from lands far away have now fallen into ruin. The Wayfarer's Guildsmen wish to change this. When the Kingdom splintered, the House of Kings in Fornost became the new seat of Royal power and the insignia of Elendil's reign were kept in this grand palace for many years. When the city fell, the place was deserted and Elendil's heirs went into hiding; bringing the signs of their power to the safety of Rivendell. The Dúnedain dwindled and the lesser men began to forget the kingdom of old except in their legends. Arnor, for many centuries not more than a name, is about to become a reality again. The House of Kings has been rebuilt and from near and far the king is calling together his peoples so that they may pledge their allegiance and be rewarded for their loyalty – and see with their own eyes, that the kingdom is real.

{anor_palantir_northern_european}Piedra de Anor
{anor_palantir_northern_european_desc}The Palantíri (sometimes translated as "Seeing Stones") are stones that can be used in communication with one another, and also to see many things across the face of the world. When its master looks in it, he can communicate with other Stones and anyone who might be looking into them.\n\nThose men who are not of Númenórean descent or have long forgotten the majesty and power of Númenor will not see the Palantir for its true value and will simply use the mighty stone to gather more money for their cause.\n\nUnder the control of the Orcs, the Palantir is put to work to steal secrets from the men of Gondor and the Elves, this knowledge is then turned to their advantage and used to improve their poor weapons and refit their warriors faster.\n\nHaving known of the power Palantir for many years and keeping one under their control in Elostirion, the Elves turn this power to communicate with their brethren all over Middle-earth and help one another in their attempts to leave or fight, as such, the Elf lord governing a Palantir will certainly have the ability to improve his warriors in battle.\n\nThe Dwarves are industrious and knowing not the true potential of this fascinating stone they look inward and use the sight of the Palantir to find the most profitable veins in the earth. With the greater output in their mining endeavours, the Dwarves are able to reduce the cost of all of their stone-works, not just at the location of the Palantir but globally!\n\nHaving worked with the Seeing Stones for hundreds of years, the descendants of Númenor can use these mighty tools as more than just glorified spies. They can turn the power of their ancestors into improving all of their warriors against the power of evil.

Having known of the power Palantir for many years and keeping one under their control in Elostirion, the Elves turn this power to communicate with their brethren all over Middle-earth and help one another in their attempts to leave or fight, as such, the Elf lord governing a Palantir will certainly have the ability to improve his warriors in battle.
{ithil_palantir_greek_desc_short}The Ithil-stone is Sauron's Palantír kept at Barad-dûr.

{teleri_barracks_desc_short}DO NOT TRANSLATE
{teleri_barracks_greek}Barracones teleri
{teleri_barracks_greek_desc}The Teleri Barracks is a simple structure that provides a dedicated space for training and accommodation of the various Lindar warriors of the Eldar. Unlike the Ñoldor and Silvan elves, the hearts of the Teleri yearn always for the sea and if they must be sent from home in times of war, then they will only settle by major water courses. Accordingly, the Teleri Barracks can only be built on the shores of the sea, on the shores of the lakes and on the banks of the following rivers:\n\nBrandywine, Bruinen, Gwathló, Carnen, Anduin, Isen, Lhûn, Harnen, Poros, Celduin and Entwash\n\nLindar battalions train faster in grasslands.
{teleri_barracks_greek_desc_short}The Teleri Barracks provides training of Lindar battalions.

Within its thick stone walls is a catacomb of corridors and rooms, protected with heavy wooden doors and iron-barred windows. Its vast armories are more than adequate for supplying under-equipped troops with fresh gear, and many hundreds of men may find rest in its extensive barracks complex. A large kitchen provides the garrison with ample food, ensuring that the impact of their presence is hardly felt by the local populace. That said, their presence will most certainly be seen. {serpent_palace_northern_european_desc}During the Second Age, Númenórean expansion reached the lands of Harad. The Black Palace was built as an administrative and military headquarters. The city that grew around the Palace was Numenors' attempt to bring order to the scattered tribes. The throne room and court are also held here. The lower level is where the palace gains its most sinister reputation. Dark passages twist their way through the city, small pockets of cold stone cells and rooms filled with devices of torture account for the true nature of the confederation. Those who have displeased the Serpent Lord, disrespected his law, or simply found themselves at the wrong place at the wrong moment, will end up victims of his deprived torturers and jailers who will ensure their suffering is immense.\n\nCoercion, subterfuge, intimidation, and torture. These are the lessons that Sauron teaches the men of the south. The Black Palace truly is a fitting tribute to the Dark Lord; an opulent husk concealing the insidious rot of evil.

{green_book_cardolan_northern_european}Cardolan
{green_book_cardolan_northern_european_desc}Cardolan is a breakaway realm of the Dúnedain kingdom of Arnor. After the death of its tenth King, Eärendur, his sons divided the kingdom into the kingdoms of Arthedain, Rhudaur and Cardolan. Cardolan stretches from the river Baranduin to the Mitheithel. Its northern border is the Great East Road, but Cardolan also claims the Weather Hills, which contain the fortress of Amon Sûl. Amon Sûl housed a Palantir, and for this reason it was also claimed by Rhudaur. This lead to a bitter conflict which continued until Rhudaur became a vassal of Angmar after the line of the Dúnedain failed there. After the final fall of Arnor, and the destruction of Angmar at the Battle of Fornost, Cardolan remained an almost unpopulated area. Cardolan was conquered in T.A. 1409 by the forces of Angmar: rather than besiege the Cardolanians major encampment atop the Barrow-downs, the twisted forces of Angmar sent evil spirits to occupy the barrows and this forced the armies of Cardolan to leave their defensive position, allowing them to be destroyed. Despite the deserted land, the Greenway still runs through the region and is used by travellers, albeit infrequently. Additionally many petty Kingdoms split off from the remnants of the realm, such as the Kingdom of Saralainn.\n\nTerreno:\nEgenyar - Praderas\nCardolan Proper - Bosque\nSwanfleet - Yermo\nFaerdor - Praderas\nLone-lands - Praderas

Properly speaking Rhovanion is the name of a small region east of Greenwood, which later was the Kingdom of Rhovanion, but the name was used for all of Wilderland by the late Third Age. The Kingdom of Rhovanion was founded before the year 490 of the Third Age by a group of Northmen who were led by a 'Prince of Rhovanion'. In Third Age 1636 the Great Plague devastated Rhovanion, killing more than half its people. This left Rhovanion weakened, and in Third Age 1851 the Wainriders overran and enslaved Rhovanion. For 43 years Rhovanion was enslaved, but in Third Age 1899 Rhovanion revolted, while Gondor attacked the Wainriders from the west. Rhovanion was freed, but left extremely weakened. Many Men of Rhovanion left for Gondor, where they were welcomed as distant relatives.\nAround 2510 a new group of Easterlings, the Balchoth, appeared, and they quickly took the old lands of Rhovanion. This was the final end of Rhovanion as an independent realm.\n\nTerreno:\nPlains of Vidugavia - Bosque\nLeofric's Bowing - Praderas\nMarches of the Northmen - Praderas\nEast Bight - Yermo\nBurnt Lands - Praderas\nLôthaur - Praderas\nRhuvan - Bosque\nPlains of Sorrow - Montañas\nOld Rhûn Road - Praderas\nWilderlands - Praderas\nMirvan - Praderas

{green_book_osgiliath_northern_european_desc}Osgiliath was the old capital city of Gondor. In its days of glory, the city featured quays to handle sea-going vessels that came up from the sea, a great stone bridge supporting houses and towers of stone, and the Dome of Stars, which housed the Osgiliath-stone, the greatest of the seven Palantíri. The beginning of the city's decline came in T.A. 1437 when it was sacked and burned, after a siege by the rebel Castamir's forces during the Kin-strife. It was during this siege that the Osgiliath-stone was lost in the River. {green_book_belfalas_northern_european_desc}Belfalas, Sindarin for 'Great Shore', forms a part of Dor-en-Ernil, or the "Prince's land". The Prince in question here is the Lord of Dol Amroth, who lives at the city bearing his name. The first Lord of Dol Amroth was Galador, son of Imrazôr the Númenórean. Imrazôr was the son of Adrahil I, who was already known as the Prince, and lived in Belfalas. At some point Imrazôr moved to the area where the elven haven of Edhellond is. According to tradition, there he married Mithrellas, a Silvan Elf of Lórien who had accompanied Nimrodel, the beloved of Lórien's king Amroth, on her journey towards Edhellond, but had become lost along with her mistress. Therefore Galador and his descendants had claim to Elven blood. After Imrazôr's death, Galador went on to found the city and later the princedom of Dol Amroth. He is counted as its first Lord. The specific date of its foundation is nowhere recounted. The large bay, stretching from Andrast in the west to the smaller bay of Umbar in the east, is named after the Belfalas peninsula.\n\nTerreno:\nDor-en-Ernil - Montañas\nCape of Belfalas - Bosque\nRiverlands - Praderas\nElf-haven - Praderas

{green_book_ethring_northern_european_desc}The Ringló Vale is a geographical feature of western Lamedon and comprises of only the river Ringló and its immediate surroundings. The region bares a lot of traffic from east and west as it houses the bridge city of Ethring, a major crossing point of the river Ringló and the main passage through the Gondorian heartlands. The city of Ethring started out as a group of merchant stalls, hastily built upon the large stone bridge. They would offer all sorts of wares to the vast numbers of people that used the bridge. Eventually they grew in wealth and began setting up taverns and smithies and operating as a key checkpoint for the east-west road. Once their wealth had become wide spread knowledge, the 'Merchants Bridge' became the target of many raids and Minas Tirith sent troops to defend the bridge. The garrison quickly erected walls, attracting scared villagers from the surrounding hamlets and villages and thus the town, as she was known in the War of the Ring, was born.\n\nTerreno:\nRingló Vale - Bosque

{green_book_cair_andros_northern_european_desc}Cair Andros is a large river-island in the Anduin River, to the east of the land of Anórien. It is held in defence against Mordor by Gondor to prevent crossings of the Great River. The island itself is long and narrow, a little over ten miles in length. At its northern end, sharp rocks split the waters of the Anduin in a bubbling foam that gave the island its name. Cair Andros is covered with trees for much of its length. Strategically, the island is of immense importance: apart from the bridge at Osgiliath, it is the only practical means for an army from the east to cross the Anduin into Gondor's heartlands. The Gondorians took this risk seriously. Amon Dîn, the first of the Beacon-hills, was set up originally to warn the citizens of Minas Tirith if Cair Andros was ever breached. Steward Túrin II built the fortress upon Cair Andros to defend the crossing indefinitely.\n\nTerreno:\nIsle of Andros - Praderas

{dragon_sanctum_desc}Rhûn is a vast and mysterious place. While it is simply known as the "East" to the people of Middle-earth, the lands surrounding Mistrand would be more accurately described as the "West" of Rhûn by the people that actually inhabit it. Like many other places in Middle-earth, it is a melting pot of ideas, cultures and beliefs. To the people of Mistrand and Rhûn, one of these beliefs is the venerance of what is understood to be "dragons" or "wyrms". Where this unusual practice originated from is unknown exactly, there may actually be powerful drakes further east or it may simply be another of Sauron's machinations to hold sway over the people here. In any case, it matters not, as this animalistic worship is widespread through Rhûnnic society, from the lower classes to the noblemen and even the Lôke-Kân himself.\n\nUnlike other traditional worship in Rhûn and beyond, there is a large emphasis placed on strength, power and one's ability to triumph over others. For this reason, the "dragon cult" is home to many skilled warriors and tacticians and is heavily intertwined throughout the nation's military. The sanctum, usually nestled underground somewhere on the outskirts of the settlement, provides both a quiet place of worship and a training ground for the cultists to spar with each other and hone their skills.

For this reason, the "dragon cult" is home to many skilled warriors and tacticians and is heavily intertwined throughout the nation's military. This vast and overbearing temple would be more aptly described as a military complex. Usually constructed far outside the walls of the settlement, perhaps as a way to further isolate and indoctrinate the worshippers of the cult, it is self-sufficient enough to provide food, bedding, equipment and materials for the training of the cult's most fearsome warriors - the Dragonswrath. Many who come here have already seen many a battle and are devoted to further improving their craft.
{dragon_temple_desc_short}A vast temple complex for the worshippers of Rhûn's "dragon cult"

{catacombs_of_furinor}Catacumbas de Fuinor
{catacombs_of_furinor_desc}After Númenor fell in the Second Age Harad was thrown into absolute chaos. The Numenorians had become decadent and cruel in their rule of tribal people, and the rift created between the rulers and surfs of the land erupted into violence when Ar-Pharazon and his corrupted Kingdom sank beneath the sea.\n\nInto this fire Sauron; newly returned from the destruction of Númenor, placed two of his most loyal and cunnning servants: Fuinor and Herumor. Black Numenorians who had proven themselves worthy of returning to Middle Earth with their chosen kin. The Black Numenorians seized on the opportunity in Harad and joined the fight on behalf of the oppressed people, blaming their own brothers for the corruption that caused so much pain in Harad. They quickly crushed and drove out the divided Faithful and King's men and established the Confederation of Harad, under the God-King Sauron the Savior. \n\nA masterful play by The Dark Lord...\n\nWhile Herumor labored to spread the worship of Sauron to all corners of Harad and snuff out the last of the Faithful from the South, Fuinor set about to weave the dreaded Hasarii into the fabric of this "empire" and establish a new and powerful arm of Sauron's rule that would stand the test of time. Underneath the Black Palace Lord Fuinor ordered a massive labyrinth of tunnels, secret prisons, and torture chambers to be constructed. The center was the new headquarters of the Hasarii; originally the first men and women who took up arms against hated Númenor they quickly became a terrible and dark force within Harad, acting as a secret police force who would take any order given to preserve the sanctity of this new state. They would become the eyes and ears of Harad's rulers and never waver in their duty to defend their God-King's chosen land. \n\nFuinor's Catacombs are where the roots of evil spread throughout Harad. It is where the condemned go to die, and the disloyal who vanish from their home or the streets now wallow in darkness. The Hasarii hold to their oaths and their loyalty to the current Serpent Lord is unwavering, for theirs is the sacred duty to ensure Harad's rulers are those who serve Sauron.

{path_of_the_benevolent}Camino del Benevolente
{path_of_the_benevolent_desc}The Second Age was one filled with strife and upheaval for the people of Harad. Colonization by the Numenorians brought with it the change of their social order and the construction of many fortified settlements and cities was seen as an encroachment upon their lands, and the great ports and aqueducts became symbolic of their lost freedom. The changes brought by Númenórean overlordship were viewed as dismantling of the tribes' heritage and Sauron played upon this belief to sow disharmony between the tribes of Harad and Númenor.\n\nHe gave one of the Rings of Power to a powerful man of Harad and offered his wisdom as a counterweight to the influence of the West. Sauron would speak of 'what was to come' and how any kind act by Númenor was only a prelude to future evil. In this way, Sauron was building up strong support among the tribes in preparation for Numenors' downfall. Sauron knew he could not defeat Númenor directly so he played this game of subterfuge until Ar-Pharazon landed his great host at Umbar and began his march into Harad. Sauron's forces fled Pharazon's army and Sauron allowed himself to be captured and taken to the great island Kingdom.\n\nAs the Numenorians became cruel and oppressive during their descent into corruption the tribes of Harad became increasingly hostile to the cultures of the West. Their leaders saw this time as proof that Sauron was correct; that the men of the West truly were evil and they began to pray for Sauron's return and they began to resist the will of their occupiers. The Hasarii began to conduct a covert war of resistance during this time.\n\nSauron's surrender was a calculated act of great cunning. His corruption of Númenor severed any hope for a peaceful coexistence between them and the Haradrim, and when the island fell the people of Harad rallied to Sauron's banner. His surrender is now seen as an act of sacrifice on behalf of his people, Numenor's destruction was proof of Sauron's divinity. This place is considered holy ground to his devoted followers and many will journey here to walk in their God-King's footsteps. Walking the Path of the Benevolent is considered a holy pilgrimage for the people of Harad, a way to connect to their God-King's journey sacrifice.

{temple_of_sauron}Sanctum de Sauron
{temple_of_sauron_desc}The worship of Sauron has been practiced in Harad since the Second Age. The Dark Lord is known as Sauron the Savior, the Protector, the Beneficent, and other titles that would make the Elves cringe in disgust. The Alter itself resembles Sauron in his fairer form before the fall of Númenor, with the people of Harad rejoicing beneath him. The traditions of the tribes have long existed intertwined with the belief that Sauron delivered them from torment and oppression at the hands of Númenor, and any written texts contradicting this claim would be considered heretical and purged.

{muhad_bazzar}Bazar muhad
{muhad_bazzar_desc}The Muhad Bazaar in Amrûn is the largest and most popular of the tribe's marketplaces in Harad. Muhad caravans have all the essentials to set up shop anywhere they find space and customers, but Amrûn's central location in Near Harad means that each of the major trade routes run through it, so it sees the most number of caravans pass through each season. The Bazaar, therefore, is never taken down. And when multiple caravans are present and selling their goods it is a marvelous sight!\n\nWhile the tribes of Harad have their domestic trade between the towns and cities of central Harad, the Muhad control the trade routes into Far-Harad and East into Khand and Rûhn. Exotic goods from all across the south and east of Middle-Earth are traded and bartered here. Spices and cotton, sugar and silks, even goods from faraway lands find their way here; furs from the Anduin Vail, jewels from Erebor, even pipeweed from the Shire! Though such luxuries are typically affordable only by the elite.\n\nDuring times of war, the Bazaar is always busy. The Muhad are responsible for the transport of plunder from the front line, and the best way for a soldier to ensure that his hard-won treasures get to his family and tribe safely is to entrust a member of the Muhad to deliver them. The loot is then typically sold and the proceeds are sent along to the soldier's tribe and family, after the Muhad take their owed percentage of course.

This is sacred ground for the dreaded Trollmen of Far Harad and any who venture here must have their blessing, if they do not wish to join the fallen.\n\nThe Mumakil travel the south in great herds, following the rain cycles that bring life to the oasis and jungles of Harad. When the old of the herd cannot travel any longer they will come here to rest one final time. {great_statue_of_sauron}Gran estatua de Sauron
{great_statue_of_sauron_desc}At last a fitting monument to his greatness; Sauron the Benevolent, has risen from the ungrateful earth to inspire all with reverence for his grace! As such the Pillar was razed and its foundation pulled from the ground.
