{kingsblood_tributary}Tributario de la sangre real
{kingsblood_tributary_desc}The Kingsblood Tributary is arguably the largest and most advanced irrigation system in Middle Earth. A product of Numenorian engineering and architectural genius, the Tributary makes use of the natural flood cycle of the Harnen river and the mineral rich run off from the Shadow Mountains to enrich and preserve the fertile soil. A massive canal system connects the inland farms to the river, with underground aquifers utilized to bring fresh water into the harsher territory via aqueducts and pressure wells. This system took over a century to create and the colonies of Numenor taught the local Haradrim the techniques they used, at first this was how the two people were able to bridge their mistrust and forge a communal relationship.\n\nHistory might have been different had it not been for the influence of Sauron and the growing ambitions of Numenor. The Haradrim tribes grew in number thanks to the massive harvests the Tributary afforded them, however their colonial overlords began to depend on the growing breadbasket and the tribes became slaves in their own farms. The tribes were also expected to maintain the Kingsblood Tributary, delving into the underground waterways to ensure it functioned properly.\n\nWhen Numenor was destroyed, and the chains of its tyranny broken, the tribes of the Haradwaith continued to maintain the Kingsblood Tributary and it remained one of the few surviving innovations from Numenor. The Serpent Tribe -Sauron’s chosen proxy rulers of Harad, have long maintained control of the vital reservoirs, basins and dikes, holding an iron grip on the agricultural bounty. This ensures the ‘Southern Multitude’ continues to thrive and remain loyal to their masters.\n\nThe bounty of the Harnen and the farms and fields it supports is enormous. The sophisticated irrigation and warm climate allow for year long planting of grains, fruits, vegetables and textiles. These goods are used to support the massive population of Harad and exports reach far and wide across the south of Middle Earth. The people who work to provide this bounty would have a fair life, if they were not beneath the iron boot of the Serpent Tribe. As it is; tribal leaders can expect any profit they make at market to be spent equipping their young men for service in Harad’s Legions.\n\nThe cruel tithe of manpower the Serpent Lord demands keeps the tribes under control and their pockets just empty enough that they will never be able to rise against him, or seek out a different way of life. The tribes have ancestral ties to their plots of land and few consider a future without the rule of Sauron, besides that the Serpent Tribe is quick to remind them of their powerlessness should any such sentiments arise. Each tribe holds a farm dependent on the Tributary, depending upon their location there could be multiple tribes tied to a particular dike or canal, thus loyalty is mutual and none would risk their lives in open rebellion and watch their fields and families wither.
{kingsblood_tributary_desc_short}A vast tributary system built to irrigate the lands surrounding Faenobel.

{petrified_forest}Bosque petrificado
{petrified_forest_desc}Where the Great Plains of Khand meet the eastern edge of Nurn is a bleak and strange place. The corruption of Mordor lingers in both air and earth; the scent of sulfur mixes with the dry, earthy grasses and clings to the wind that slips between the crags of the Mountains of Shadow. Here, in this realm between realms, lies the place the Variags call Kyz’huf Haruk the "Stone Grove". What remains is the skeleton of an ancient forest, petrified by time. Once living trees now stand frozen, their trunks turned to stone, their twisted limbs clawing at the sky or as shattered glass on the ground.\n\nTo the Variags, the grove is not dead. Elders and shamans come here bearing offerings of ash, salt, and bone, to pay homage to the elements and seek communion with the spirits of this place. They believe the trees still harbor echoes of life, that within their silent forms stirs a power that can bridge the gap between this world and the next. Some scoff at these old beliefs, calling them superstition clung to by the weak and the weary. But cynicism holds little sway in Kyz’huf Haruk, where pilgrims report visions of the fallen, or hear the whispers of long-dead kin carried on the still air.\n\nEven the orcs avoid this place. If they wander too close, driven by curiosity or command, they do not return to their camps. The Variags who come here do not welcome them—the grove, it seems, does not suffer their presence. There is a silence here that does not merely blanket the land, but watches. A weight in the air that bends the will and stills the tongue. To trespass without reverence is to invite death.\n\nSome among the Variags claim the grove remembers. That the shapes of the trees shift when no one is looking, that the stones themselves hum with the breath of the past. Shadows stretch too long beneath the canopy, and light filters down in strange colors, as if strained through memory. Kyz’huf Haruk is not just a place of death—it is a place of listening, of remembrance. And in the stillness of its stony embrace, there is a darkened sense of peace impossible to escape.
{petrified_forest_desc_short}Kyz’huf Haruk - the Stone Grove

{harad_oasis}Ouwe al al-Hazin
{harad_oasis_desc}Deep within the sun-scorched dunes of Far Harad, hidden beyond shifting sands and mirage-laden wastes, lies Ouwe al-Hazin — the Jewel of the Deep Desert. This secret oasis is an important key to the Muhad caravan network that weave through the vast wastes into the mysterious lands beyond Far Harad. It is a lifeline for those journeying toward the distant south.\n\nThe path to the Ouwe is treacherous and it's precise location is known only among the Muhad and their guides. To the unprepared, the desert is an unforgiving expanse where the very air shimmers lies and with the heat despair. Here the dunes stretch endlessly, swallowing trails with the winds of each passing night and bringing madness to those who do not know the ways the desert. But for those privy to its secrets, the promise of water, shade and renewal awaits.\n\nThe Ouwe al-Hazin is a beautiful wonder of nature, where an ancient underground river feeds crystalline pools, cool to the touch even in the height of summer. Towering palm trees cast shifting shadows, their roots drinking deep of the hidden veins below. Lush reeds and flowering plants thrive along the banks, life holds a defiant strength here surrounded by the deadly sands. Strange birds nest in the cliffs that cradle the oasis, their cries echoing in the stillness, while nocturnal beasts emerge as the sun sets, lapping at the water's edge.\n\nThe Muhad guard this place fiercely, for it is not merely a haven—it is a pilar for their way of life. Caravaners who earn their favor may be permitted to rest here, but outsiders who stumble upon it unbidden seldom leave with their lives. The Muhad protect the Oasis and its natural balance, knowing that were it to ever dry and wither their ability to survive the long journey through the wastes.
{harad_oasis_desc_short}A secret oasis hidden in the deep deserts of Harad.

{camp_karazom}Campamento Karazom
{camp_karazom_desc}Camp Karazom has a long history that began during the early third age, when Gondor established its border along the northern Harnen. The Haradrim were ambitious during this time and they established many camps and forts along the northern shore, attempting to find a permanent beachhead into Harondor. Karazom was the most successful of these and many raiding parties ventured from here to plunder the Gondorian holdings. Several tribes migrated here in the hope of claiming new lands to settle.\n\nWhen Harad was broken by their failed siege of Umbar the leaders of Karazom offered their surrender, promising to obey Gondor’s laws and pay its taxes. It became a modest settlement during Gondor’s rule over Harad from 1015 until the Kin Strife of 1432. It was during the Kin Strife that Karazom rejoined  Harad and broke away from Gondor’s rule. It served as a frontline base and was razed and rebuilt multiple times in the following centuries, eventually Harad gained enough ground that Karazom become a supply base for the Haradrim. After Harad’s defeat at the battle of the Poros many of the survivors were banished from Faen’obel to Karazom because of some perceived ‘failure’ that had caused such a terrible loss. Those survivors became powerful figures for potential independent tribes in Harondor and caused their fair share of trouble for the Serpent Tribe during the last century.\n\nThe Tribes that originally settled here endured this war by offering any goods or service they can with whomever is in power. Karazom boasts a great boarding house for travelers with drink and entertainment available even for those less fortunate. Soldiers and warriors are often parted from their coin with a clever sleight of hand, or an ill-fated wager. There is a reputation for discretion and the sale of information that attracts many unsavory characters. A useful place for whomever finds themselves on the throne of power in these lands.
{camp_karazom_desc_short}An old camp now transformed into a bustling border town.

{bastion_of_the_god_king}Bastión del rey dios
{bastion_of_the_god_king_desc}The Bastion is not a single building or monument, but rather a complete reshaping of the city. A new purpose for the former capital of Gondor, now held in the hands of the noble sons of Harad. Minas Tirith will become the center of Sauron's next war; the complete conquest of middle earth. Harad shall be given a leading role, as a reward for its victories, and so the armies of shadow shall flock to the banner of the Serpent, which shall march forth in the Dark Lord's name.\n\nThe Bastion stands upon the ruins of the lower district. The common homes that were not destroyed by the invasion were razed to the ground and the rubble cleared to begin construction. Several massive barracks were erected, large enough to accommodate thousands of warriors, while tunnels were dug out beneath the city to allows for even more space to be filled. Training grounds and drilling fields were made available with live prisoners to be used as the commanding officers saw fit. Men train and live in the barracks above, while Orcs are lodged below. Multiple warehouses store enough supplies to feed the legions lodge and pass through on their way to greater conquests.\n\nWhile the people of Harad could make good use of what is left of Minas Tirith; scarcely hours after the conquest was completed, dark figures road to the Serpent Lord's holdings and secret dealings too place to ensure that the fallen city aligned with Sauron's vision for middle earth. The grandeur of the White City is discarded to make way for the machine of war. No gardens are left, no pleasant spaces or quiet streets, the only sounds the hammering of smiths, the stench of blood and iron, and the marching boots of the Dark Lord's armies.
{bastion_of_the_god_king_desc_short}The lower city rebuilt into a massive military complex.

{crimson_haven}El puerto carmesí
{crimson_haven_desc}The Crimson Haven is the beating heart of a vast shipbuilding enterprise, a keystone in the ascendant might of Harad's new Black Armada. The deep natural harbor of Dol Amroth, once a bastion of Gondorian strength, now serves as a crucible for Haradrim and Umbar expansion into the northern seas. The cliffs that once bore proud towers have been carved into a labyrinth of pulleys, chains, and great iron cranes, allowing cargo, plunder, and provisions to be swiftly loaded and unloaded with ruthless efficiency. The coastline itself has been reshaped—trenches and artificial inlets carved deep into the shore, allowing warships of every class to nestle side by side, ready to launch at a moment's notice.\n\nA city of warehouses sprawls around the docks, their vast interiors brimming with stolen goods, naval supplies, and the raw timber hewn from the conquered forests of Gondor. Beside them, the dry docks thunder with the ceaseless clamor of hammer and saw, where the great ships of the Black Armada take shape under the watchful gaze of their cruel masters. The surrounding villages and townships have been emptied of their people; now, they labor beneath the lash, toiling night and day to feed this ever-hungry war machine.\n\nAbove it all, Tirith Aear looms like a fell beacon, its once-proud bell now a sinister call to arms. No longer does it serve as a watchful guardian of Gondor's shores—instead, its tolling draws raiders and pirates from across the south, answering the Dark Lord's summons to war.

{pelargir_slave_market_desc}With the conquest of Pelargir our forces have opened up a direct line of trade to Harad. ; Khand Landmarks
{great_khans_pasture}Pastos del gran Khan
{great_khans_pasture_desc}The Great Plains of Khand stretch as far as the eye can see, a seemingly endless expanse of undulating browns and yellows, dotted with wildflowers of fiery orange. This vast plain hums with the subtle song of life, insects and rodents dash beneath the grass canopy, going to ground when they feel the thunderous drumming of hooves as the wild herds gallop across the land.\n\nThese herds, sleek and muscular, are a kaleidoscope of color and breed, from black-coated stallions to dappled mares, their manes flying like banners as they race with wild abandon. Legends say that the horses of the plains are born of the wind itself, it is from these herds that the Khan secures his mounts—beasts unmatched in speed, endurance, and spirit, each one a treasure and a symbol of Khand's untamed power.\n\nThe herds will make their way through the plains to sheltered natural pastures. In these places the air is sharp and clear, carrying the rich, earthy scent of green grass, a rare sight on the hot and humid plains. The land rises and falls in subtle waves, broken only by the occasional solitary tree or rocky outcrop that offers shade and shelter. Streams of crystal-clear water carve meandering paths through these pastures, their banks trampled smooth by the uncountable numbers of horses that come to drink.\n\nHere, the Khan of Khand commands his riders to find their mounts and break them. The Variags live in a communal harmony with these herds, ensuring that they are protected and allowed to breed before any new mounts are taken. These horses are the lifeblood of the Clan and the Khan commands thet no outsider dare interfere with them, so integral are these herds to the Variags. Young warriors' rite of passage involves selecting a horse to break and they will return them here to breed, when they have grown too old they will bring them to the pasture to die amongst their kin.\n\nIf the Khan decided that tradition was to be discarded the Variags could raise a host of riders that would break the world! But such action would devastate these herds and shatter their bond with their benefactors.
{great_khans_pasture_desc_short}The Great Khan's personal pastures for rearing horses.

{khand_border_tribes}Tribus de las fronteras de Khand
{khand_border_tribes_desc}In the eastern part of Harad, the land turns from the rich river basin to the rocky hills and savanna of west Khand. The tribes that live here are scattered throughout the region and many of them are nomadic by necessity, traveling with the herds and following the rains to find grazing pastures. At times the Haradrim have laid claim to the vast region and come into conflict with the Variags of Khand for the territory. Likewise, the Variags have seen the expansion of Harad as a threat to their autonomy. War has resulted in little gain for either side and in the later years of the Third Age, the Serpent Lord proposed a settlement between the Haradrim and the Variag warriors who dwell here.\n\nThe offer was that both sides would 'share' the land, and the tribal people that live here. The Variags could raid as they saw fit, so long as they established no permanent settlements, and Harad would provide a safe gateway for trade of the savanna's resources, so long as they imposed no direct rule. This has led to positive relations between Khand and Harad, and gives the Serpent Lord a few loyal allies in the far east, insurance if Khand should ever drift away from Sauron.\n\nThe ones that do not benefit are the tribes caught between these two powers. They are raided and forced to pay tribute in gold, furs, food, and sometimes their own kin to simply exist. They are a people with no rights nor self-determination, owing their allegiance to neither faction means that they are constantly prayed upon and long for the day they can shake off this evil.

; Imlad Carnen, Eastern Harondor

{shadow_mountain_mines_desc}These mines were established after the fall of Sauron in the Second Age, when Gondor had reached the height of its power. The mines remained prosperous until the Kin Strife when Gondor's civil war tore the country apart. The mines were abandoned and left unused until a restoration attempt in the second half of the Third Age that ultimately failed when the Haradrim invaded Harondor.\n\nBecause of their proximity to Mordor the mines were never considered to be worth the effort for Gondor to reclaim. ; Haudhanûr
{battle_of_the_poros}Batalla del Poros
{battle_of_the_poros_desc}In the year 2885 of the Third Age, during the reign of Steward Túrin II, the Haradrim amassed a vast army under the command of the Serpent Lord Zelkara and assailed Southern Ithilien. The Haradrim had enjoyed a successful conquest of Harondor and were eager to continue their fight and march upon Osgiliath. It was at the Crossings of Poros where Túrin II and King Folwine of Rohan mustered their armies for defense against the Southern storm. The Haradrim outnumbered the Gondorians and their allies ten to one and were so confident of victory they sang and chanted and jeered at their foe as they surged across the river.\n\nThe allied troops had destroyed the bridge and watched as their foe became weighted down by the water, content to wait until they had exhausted themselves at their crossing before making their strike. The cavalry of Rohan proved to be devastating to the Haradrim, while not wanting for spears, they could not withstand the powerful charges King Folcwine unleashed against them. The Haradrim were cut down by a third before they changed their tactics, bringing in archers to cover their advance. This was when Gondor brought up their heavy troops in shining steel, the simple arrows of the Haradrim were near useless and Gondor held the line as the enemy crashed upon them.\n\nIn a fury, Serpent Lord Zelkara sent in his mighty Mumakil to crush the Gondorian line. The raging beasts trampled friend and foe alike and Zelkara joined in the fray. That was when King Folcwine's sons Fastred and Folcred delivered a great charge to relieve the wavering Gondorians. The two brothers carved through the ranks of Serpent Guards and hamstrung the great Mumak. Serpent Lord Zelkara was crushed beneath his own monster, but the two heroes were surrounded by the enemy and were overwhelmed. The men of Rohan let out a roar of defiance at the sight of their fallen leaders and surged forward into the confused Haradrim and they broke into a mass rout, trampling each other as they fled back across the Poros.\n\nThe battle was a victory, but a costly one for the men of the west. Gondor's army was ravaged and Rohan's king lost both of his sons. It was a day of great sacrifice for the free people of Middle Earth. For Harad; the defeat at the Poros was devastating. Their conquest of Harondor was undone, the Serpent Tribe was plunged into chaos, and it would take over a century for the Haradrim to recover the loss of manpower.
{battle_of_the_poros_desc_short}Sight of the costly victory for Gondor and Rohan at the crossing of the Poros river.

While Harondor once held itself as an independent power boasting of its own military and proud tradition of resisting the rise of Mordor and its allies, now any sense of hope is gone, and its people do what they must to survive.\n\nAs such; the life of a mercenary may be quite appealing for some in Harondor. ; Tirithoros. North Harondor
{ruined_beacon_of_harondor}Almenara de Harondor en ruinas
{ruined_beacon_of_harondor_desc}At the height of Gondor's power, Harondor was a proud frontier province with great potential in its mineral wealth and agriculture. A network of beacons was built to provide Gondor with a warning system if ever Harondor came under attack. Using these beacons; the army of Gondor was able to effectively respond to threats of invasion in the south. It also made these beacons primary targets for any potential invader.\n\nIn the Third Age Harondor suffered a score of conflicts that resulted in the province becoming fractured. The beacons helped in the defense of the province, but in the end, Harondor was broken by the ceaseless enemy. The beacons were snuffed out, and this one was the last to fall. Heavily fortified, it's light was able to reach across the Anduin to Pelargir and from there the alarm could reach Minas Tirith in a matter of hours.\n\nThis beacon was destroyed before the War of the Ring, when a massive Haradrim army pressed northward towards the Poros and its leader ordered that the beacon be destroyed. A sneak attack was planned to eliminate the possibility of reinforcements, and under cover of darkness; the Haradrim set about to sabotage the beacon. During their attack, however, a fire broke out and consumed the beacon, ultimately alerting Gondor to the impending invasion. The result was the last battle at the Poros crossing that was a victory for Gondor.

The Hasarii became a part of Sauron's dominion over Harad, enforcing his laws and punishing any who dared act against them. There were some who saw this new 'freedom' for the true tyranny that it was, and they gathered here in the late years of the second age. Here they attempted the same resistance against Sauron's rule that he had taught to the Hasarii. {edhellond_harbour}Puerto élfico de Edhellond

{halls_of_scorgrim_basic_southern_european}Salones de Skorgrím
{halls_of_scorgrim_basic_southern_european_desc}Skorgrím was both a great warrior and general who lead the Dwarves of Nogrod to victory against the elves in the First Age. He ordered the sacking of Menegroth, the Thousand Caves which was home to king Thingol of the Sindarin elves and fought fiercely at the Battle of Sarn Athrad. To many dwarves, he represents a dark time in their history but for the true and enlightened dwarf, he is a great hero and is revered as a symbol of the Old Times, when Dwarves showed their might and did not bow to the demands of Men and Elves. Building a hall here in Buzra-Dum, dedicated to his name and memory will both inspire the younger Dwarves to take up arms as well as entice great swordsmiths who still remember the Old Times to flock here.
{halls_of_scorgrim_basic_southern_european_short}Salones de Skorgrím
